options.name: Sparse working directory
options.description: The default clone materializes only a limited subset of repository files, initially favoring root content and user-directed expansion.

options.name: Full working-directory population
options.description: An explicit full-clone mode materializes all tracked files for workflows requiring complete local visibility.

options.name: Virtualized filesystem repository access
options.description: Uses a virtualized filesystem to expose only needed repository content while supporting very large working trees.

options.name: Non-virtualized large-repository support
options.description: Scales very large repositories without requiring a virtualized filesystem.

options.name: Git fsmonitor with Watchman
options.description: Git uses fsmonitor together with Watchman to obtain changed paths and restrict index inspection.

options.name: Git-aware custom filesystem watcher
options.description: A watcher integrated with Git understands ignore patterns and avoids scans that a general-purpose watcher cannot eliminate.

options.name: General-purpose Watchman monitoring
options.description: Using Watchman as the principal watcher without Git-specific awareness was declined in favor of a Git-aware implementation.

options.name: Background remote fetching
options.description: Hourly fetches synchronize client repositories without requiring users to initiate every update.

options.name: Opt-in background Git maintenance
options.description: Maintenance is moved out of infeasible foreground garbage-collection workflows into an easy, opt-in background process.

options.name: Background commit-graph maintenance
options.description: Commit graphs are generated and updated outside foreground fetches and commands to preserve large-repository responsiveness.

options.name: Per-repository maintenance registration
options.description: Repositories are explicitly registered to enable local configuration and background maintenance, with lifecycle controls for pausing or unregistering.

options.name: Scalar-managed background Git maintenance
options.description: Uses a client manager to configure repositories and run maintenance work in the background.

options.name: Incremental background maintenance
options.description: Perform repository upkeep incrementally in background processes to limit client resource impact.

options.name: Foreground maintenance deferral
options.description: Expensive garbage collection, commit-graph writing, and configuration work are moved out of user-facing Git commands.

options.name: Single-command maintenance orchestration
options.description: Running configuration, fetching, graph updates, and cleanup together.

options.name: Foreground automatic garbage collection
options.description: Run threshold-triggered repository garbage collection synchronously at the end of user commands.

options.name: Automatic garbage-collection suppression
options.description: Disable automatic garbage collection and defer all cleanup indefinitely.

options.name: Complete object-data rewriting
options.description: Rewrite and recompress all repository objects during garbage collection.

options.name: Automatic metadata maintenance
options.description: Commit-graphs, multi-pack indexes, and related Git structures are updated automatically as repository history and packs grow.

options.name: Compressed Git index
options.description: The local index is compressed to reduce repository metadata size.

options.name: Hidden remote-reference namespace
options.description: Remote references are retained under a separate namespace for reachability and commit-graph work without changing user-visible tracking branches.

options.name: Incremental split commit-graph format
options.description: Split commit-graph files incrementally update reachable-commit metadata while limiting repeated maintenance cost.

options.name: Disabled ahead-behind calculation
options.description: Disables ahead-behind computation to avoid unnecessary large-repository client work.

options.name: Upstream core-Git feature integration
options.description: Moves Scalar-developed performance and maintenance capabilities into upstream Git for broad client availability.

options.name: Custom Git client dependency
options.description: Client acceleration depends on distributing a Git build containing features not yet available in the standard client.

options.name: Migration from Scalar to core Git
options.description: Move users from a Scalar management layer to an improved core Git client as upstream capabilities expand.

options.name: Automatic Git performance configuration
options.description: Applies recommended performance settings automatically to reduce manual large-repository tuning.

options.name: Advanced Git performance features disabled by default
options.description: Leaves compatibility-sensitive performance capabilities off unless users or tooling enable them.

options.name: Trace-driven Git performance diagnosis
options.description: Uses traces and user feedback to locate large-repository command bottlenecks before tuning the client.

options.name: Write-ahead-log authority
options.description: The WAL is the authoritative record, avoiding synchronization with an external reference or object database.

options.name: External relational reference database
options.description: A relational database storing references to blob-hosted packfiles was rejected because of operational and consistency risks.

options.name: Eventual-consistency repository views
options.description: Allow replicas to serve repository states that may temporarily omit recently pushed commits.

options.name: Fully consistent replica set
options.description: Keeping all replicas consistent for reads and higher-level operations.

options.name: Consistency and partition-tolerance priority
options.description: Prioritizing consistency and partition tolerance over availability during failures.

options.name: Per-write voting protocol
options.description: Each write is resolved directly through a replica voting protocol rather than through a separately elected primary.

options.name: Primary-copy write ordering
options.description: A single primary whose arrival order dictates writes was explicitly rejected as Spokes’ coordination model.

options.name: Linearized repository pushes
options.description: All pushes receive one ordered history of repository mutations under concurrent production activity.

options.name: Deterministic preferred writer selection
options.description: A deterministic healthy-path writer reduces contention while failover permits another server to accept the operation.

options.name: Per-repository reference-update latency budget
options.description: A few-hundred-millisecond budget supporting several reference updates per second.

options.name: Read-preserving write optimization
options.description: Improving reference-update speed without slowing predominantly read workloads.

options.name: Consensus-free CAS write coordination
options.description: Concurrent pushes update shared log state through atomic compare-and-swap without electing a repository primary.

options.name: Three-phase replicated reference transactions
options.description: Replicas prepare, validate, commit, or atomically roll back Git reference updates as one coordinated transaction.

options.name: Majority-based exclusive write locking
options.description: Acquires exclusive locks on a majority of replicas to serialize conflicting repository mutations.

options.name: Proxy-mediated replication fan-out
options.description: Routes each push through a proxy that transparently forwards the update to multiple repository replicas.

options.name: Advanced consensus for reduced coordination rounds
options.description: Uses a more advanced consensus approach to reduce distant-replica coordination round trips.

options.name: Low-latency replica communication
options.description: Keeps replicas sufficiently close to sustain high-rate coordinated repository updates.

options.name: Overlapped replica coordination work
options.description: Performs independent lock, checksum, and database work while waiting for network operations.

options.name: Reference-transaction-focused synchronization
options.description: Concentrate coordinated synchronization on small reference transactions while distributing larger packfiles without consensus.

options.name: Retiring-server removal from active replica counts
options.description: Removes retiring servers from active counts while retaining service access and triggering under-replication repair.

options.name: Majority-based durable writes
options.description: A write becomes durable only after succeeding on a majority of replicas.

options.name: Three-replica repository durability
options.description: Maintains at least three repository copies to survive server failures while preserving availability and durable writes.

options.name: Rack-separated replica placement
options.description: Places replicas in distinct racks so rack-wide infrastructure failures do not remove all durable copies.

options.name: Single-extra-copy durability scheme
options.description: Uses one additional replica to survive a single-node failure without the stronger serialization properties of a majority.

options.name: Fixed replication floor
options.description: Requiring a minimum replica count even for small or lightly used repositories.

options.name: Arbitrary replica count
options.description: Scaling read capacity by deploying an arbitrary number of replicas.

options.name: S3-backed WAL durability
options.description: Using S3 WAL updates as the durability path for repository writes.

options.name: S3 Express One Zone WAL storage
options.description: Using S3 Express One Zone to reduce WAL update latency.

options.name: Automated replica repair
options.description: Losing or lagging replicas are quarantined, repaired automatically, and returned to service without user-visible unavailability.

options.name: Elastic N-to-N re-replication
options.description: After server loss, surviving repository copies are copied in parallel to replacement replicas across the cluster.

options.name: UDP gossip replica notification
options.description: Use optimistic unreliable gossip to notify replicas while allowing independent recovery from durable source state.

options.name: Pet-style repository operations
options.description: Treating repository copies as individually important operational assets.

options.name: Primary-only repository compaction
options.description: CPU-intensive repacking runs only on the primary and its compaction events propagate through the WAL.

options.name: Replica-side repository repacking
options.description: Independent repacking on replicas was rejected because it duplicates CPU work and can trigger availability-threatening maintenance conflicts.

options.name: Idle-replica disk garbage collection
options.description: Remove inactive repository materializations from replica disks and recreate them from durable log data on demand.

options.name: Incremental multi-pack-index repacking
options.description: Repack selected batches of small packs and expire unreferenced packs in separate safe phases.

options.name: Replica-wide compacted-data replication
options.description: Replicating compacted Git data to other nodes for consistent reads.

options.name: Loose-object cleanup
options.description: Remove loose objects during repository maintenance to reduce object-file overhead.

options.name: Delta-compressed packfiles
options.description: Store Git objects in delta-compressed packfiles for space-efficient repository representation.

options.name: Single-pack repository repacking
options.description: Rewrite accumulated repository data into one consolidated packfile during garbage collection.

options.name: Closest up-to-date replica routing
options.description: Fetches and clones use the nearest replica known to be current.

options.name: Geographically replicated Git reads
options.description: Distributed replicas serve Git reads for users near regional or enterprise hosts.

options.name: Non-voting geo-replicated hosts
options.description: Geo-replicated hosts serve reads without participating in write quorums, preserving push availability during temporary reachability failures.

options.name: Operation-triggered replica failover
options.description: Failed repository operations trigger trying lower-preference replicas without waiting for centralized health detection.

options.name: Advisory replica demotion
options.description: Repeated failures lower a replica's preference while retaining it as a fallback rather than removing it outright.

options.name: External repository-to-machine routing table
options.description: Tracking repository replica locations in an external database.

options.name: Any synchronized replica read routing
options.description: Route reads to any replica when accepted writes make all replicas current.

options.name: Per-server failure and load views
options.description: Application servers maintain local file-server failure views, while heartbeats poll load and signal recovery.

options.name: Live-traffic failure detection
options.description: Infers server liveness from live application traffic to route requests around unavailable replicas.

options.name: Per-application-server failure detection
options.description: Lets each application server independently determine replica liveness through reachability checks and heartbeats.

options.name: Three-consecutive-failure offline threshold
options.description: Mark a server offline only after three consecutive request failures.

options.name: Filesystem-level repository distribution
options.description: Distribute Git data through a filesystem layer rather than changing Git or packfile handling.

options.name: NFS-backed centralized repository storage
options.description: Place repositories on a centralized network filesystem shared by application instances.

options.name: Git-level distribution
options.description: Distribute or modify Git itself as the repository data distribution mechanism.

options.name: Git-and-rsync file-server replication
options.description: Combine Git and rsync to replicate, repair, and rebalance repositories across file servers.

options.name: Git application-level repository replication
options.description: Replicates repository updates at the Git application level rather than at filesystem block boundaries.

options.name: Filesystem block-level replication
options.description: Replicates storage blocks independently of Git repository operations.

options.name: HTTP server over on-disk repository copy
options.description: Places a conventional HTTP daemon directly in front of an on-disk repository copy.

options.name: RPC-based repository operations
options.description: Exposing remote repository operations through an RPC layer.

options.name: Packfile-level application replication
options.description: Replicate repository data at the packfile/application layer while retaining ordinary Git repositories.

options.name: S3-distributed compacted packs
options.description: Replicas download already-compacted packfiles from S3 instead of performing local repacking.

options.name: Distributed object-level repository storage
options.description: Git objects are placed in distributed key-value or DHT storage behind a storage abstraction rather than repository-local packfiles.

options.name: Packfile-based repository storage
options.description: Stores Git code and metadata in compressed packfiles as the repository storage representation.

options.name: Packfile-based Git networking
options.description: Uses packfiles as the transfer representation for Git pushes and fetches.

options.name: Filesystem dependence of packfiles
options.description: Requires large binary packfiles to reside on a filesystem for Git access.

options.name: Whole-file local pack caching
options.description: Caching complete packfiles locally to avoid random remote access.

options.name: Co-located local repository storage
options.description: Keep repository copies on local storage alongside the application server or on local NVMe disks.

options.name: Centralized repository hosting
options.description: Expose a shared centralized host while repositories retain distributed-version-control semantics.

options.name: Distributed repository architecture
options.description: Retain distributed repository capabilities for offline work, delayed pushes, and decentralized maintainer workflows.

options.name: Rendezvous-hashed stateless repository placement
options.description: Routes repositories through location-independent, stateless placement so any server can resolve repository ownership consistently.

options.name: Single-machine repository placement
options.description: Keeping each repository copy on only one hosting machine.

options.name: Distant replica placement
options.description: Placing replicas farther apart geographically.

options.name: Co-located filesystem replicas
options.description: Keeping filesystem replicas geographically close together.

options.name: Horizontal application scaling
options.description: Scale repository-serving application instances horizontally while providing shared access to repository data.

options.name: Cloud-portable object-storage deployment
options.description: Durable repository storage uses an S3-compatible interface while remaining deployable across cloud providers.

options.name: Unsafe write acceptance
options.description: Accepting writes without committing them to the required durable copies.

options.name: Sibling source-and-build directory layout
options.description: Place source in a nested repository directory so generated build outputs can remain in sibling directories.

options.name: Direct Git-compatible clone path
options.description: Transfer ordinary Git repository data directly without a client-specific repository representation.

options.name: GVFS object-transfer protocol
options.description: Transfers repository objects selectively instead of requiring a complete object copy before work begins.

options.name: Central-server coupling for missing objects
options.description: Relies on a central host to provide objects absent from the local partial repository.

options.name: Commit-and-tree-only initial clone
options.description: Initially downloads commits and trees while omitting other Git objects until they are needed.

options.name: On-demand object downloading
options.description: Fetches missing Git objects dynamically when local commands require them.

options.name: Co-located cache-server proxying
options.description: Proxies object requests through nearby caches to reduce distance and central-host load.

options.name: GVFS-protocol cloning through Azure Repos
options.description: Uses the GVFS protocol when cloning from Azure Repos for extremely large repositories.

options.name: Partial clone
options.description: Transfers a selectively complete repository to reduce clone time and local object storage.

options.name: GVFS protocol excluded from standard Git
options.description: Keeps the GVFS protocol out of the standard Git client in favor of the standardized partial-clone approach.

options.name: GVFS without cache server for small repositories
options.description: Deploying GVFS protocol without cache infrastructure for small repositories.

options.name: Random reboot testing
options.description: Test server resilience by randomly rebooting file servers during active operations.

options.name: Quiescing before server reboot
options.description: Temporarily stop accepting new reads before reboot while waiting for active operations to finish.

options.name: Rack-level maintenance zones
options.description: Treat racks as availability zones and process one rack as the maintenance unit.

options.name: Rack-by-rack reboot sequencing
options.description: Complete reboot work in one rack before proceeding to the next rack.

options.name: Five-server reboot concurrency limit
options.description: Limit simultaneous server reboots within a rack to five.

options.name: Unplanned server unplugging
options.description: Remove a server abruptly without quiescing or coordinating active repository operations.

options.name: Crash-compatible clean shutdown
options.description: Reuse crash and permanent-failure handling mechanisms for intentional server departure.

options.name: Graceful completion of in-progress reads
options.description: Allow active reads, including long clones, to finish before server reboot.

options.name: Continued write replication during quiescing
options.description: Continue replicating writes to a quiescing server while reads drain.

options.name: Continuous repository checksum tracking
options.description: Maintaining checksums to detect invalid or corrupted repository copies.

options.name: Incremental replica checksum maintenance
options.description: Update a replica-state checksum algebraically when references change instead of recomputing it from scratch.

options.name: Full replica checksum recomputation
options.description: Recompute the checksum from every reference after each repository update.
